title: A compatible graded cohomology action is finite by the relative-spectrum argument
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $B=\bigoplus_{k\ge0}B_k$ a commutative graded $A$-algebra (the $B_k$ are $A$-submodules with $B_kB_l\subseteq B_{k+l}$ and $1\in B_0$, the structure map $A\to B$ landing in $B_0$) which is a finite type $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism], and write $f^\sharp(a)\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ for the image of $a\in A$. Let $(\mathcal G_m)_{m\ge0}$ be quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules [pqf-def-coherent], and for all $k,m\ge0$ and $b\in B_k$ let $\mu^{(m)}_b:\mathcal G_m\to\mathcal G_{m+k}$ be an $\mathcal O_X$-linear map [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], such that: (i) $\mu^{(m)}_{b+b'}=\mu^{(m)}_b+\mu^{(m)}_{b'}$ for $b,b'\in B_k$; (ii) $\mu^{(m+l)}_b\circ\mu^{(m)}_{b'}=\mu^{(m)}_{bb'}$ for $b\in B_k$, $b'\in B_l$; (iii) for $a\in A$ with image $a\cdot1\in B_0$, $\mu^{(m)}_{a\cdot1}$ is multiplication by $f^\sharp(a)$ on $\mathcal G_m$; (iv) (finite type) $X$ is covered by open sets $U$ for each of which there are finitely many integers $d_1,\dots,d_r\ge0$ and sections $s_i\in\mathcal G_{d_i}(U)$ such that for every $m\ge0$, every open $V\subseteq U$ and every $t\in\mathcal G_m(V)$, each point of $V$ has an open neighbourhood $W\subseteq V$ on which $t|_W=\sum_{i:\,d_i\le m}\sum_jc_{ij}\,\mu^{(d_i)}_{b_{ij}}(s_i)|_W$ for finitely many $c_{ij}\in\mathcal O_X(W)$ and $b_{ij}\in B_{m-d_i}$. (These data are the same as a quasi-coherent graded module $\bigoplus_m\mathcal G_m$ of finite type over the graded $\mathcal O_X$-algebra $f^*\widetilde B$, $b\in B_k$ acting through its pulled-back global section.) Fix p >= 0 and put M_m=H^p(X,G_m) [pqf-def-cohomology]. Let mod be any B-module structure on the additive direct sum M of the M_m, such that for every b in B_k and x in M_m, b acting on the degree-m inclusion of x is the degree-(m+k) inclusion of H^p(mu_m(b))(x). Then M with this specified mod is finite over B [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. The compatibility hypothesis is imposed on this very mod, not on a different existentially quantified action.

proof.text: Put $X'=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}B$, with projections $\pi:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to\operatorname{Spec}B$. Since $f$ is proper, $f'$ is proper by base change [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b). Since $B$ is finite type over the Noetherian ring $A$, it is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is Noetherian, and the proper map $f'$ is of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism], so $X'$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. In particular $X$ and $X'$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

source.place: Lemma 0897 (lemma-graded-finiteness), proof lines 5267-5279; Morphisms 01W4, Algebra 00FN, Morphisms 01T6

proof.text: Write $\mathcal B=f^*\widetilde B$ and $\mathcal G=\bigoplus_{m\ge0}\mathcal G_m$, with multiplication by a homogeneous $b\in B_k$ given by $\mu_b^{(m)}$. Conditions (i) and (ii) make this an action of the graded algebra $B$; (iii) identifies its degree-zero $A$-action with the $\mathcal O_X$-module action through $f^\sharp$. On an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}C\subseteq X$, quasi-coherence gives $\mathcal G_m|_U=\widetilde{G_m}$ for $G_m=\mathcal G_m(U)$ [pqf-def-coherent]. Localization commutes with direct sums, so $\mathcal G|_U=\widetilde{\bigoplus_mG_m}$; the same calculation identifies $\mathcal B|_U$ with the tilde of $B\otimes_AC$. The action maps localize, hence $\mathcal G$ is quasi-coherent as a $\mathcal B$-module. The local homogeneous generators $s_i$ in (iv) give a surjection $\mathcal B|_U^{\oplus r}\to\mathcal G|_U$: every section in a homogeneous summand is locally a sum of the stipulated $b_{ij}s_i$, and every section of $\mathcal G$ is locally a finite sum of homogeneous sections. Thus $\mathcal G$ has finite type over $\mathcal B$.

proof.text: The base-change description of relative spectrum [lem-weil-pbc-relative-spec-base-change](2), applied to $\widetilde B$ on $\operatorname{Spec}A$, identifies $X'$ over $X$ with $\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_X(\mathcal B)$. Therefore $\pi$ is affine and $\pi_*\mathcal O_{X'}\cong\mathcal B$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec](2). By the affine module correspondence [lem-weil-pbc-affine-module-correspondence](2), the quasi-coherent $\mathcal B$-module $\mathcal G$ uniquely corresponds to a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{X'}$-module $\mathcal G'$ with $\pi_*\mathcal G'\cong\mathcal G$ as $\mathcal B$-modules. Its finite-type property follows from [lem-weil-pbc-affine-module-finite-type], applied to the generators of step 2. Since $X'$ is locally Noetherian by step 1, finite type and quasi-coherent imply $\mathcal G'$ coherent [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth].

proof.text: Because $f'$ is proper over the affine Noetherian base $\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $\mathcal G'$ is coherent, [lem-pc-coherent-hi] (its 02O6 clause) makes $H^p(X',\mathcal G')$ a finite $B$-module. Since $\pi$ is affine and $\mathcal G'$ quasi-coherent, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-cohomology-edge] gives the canonical isomorphism $H^p(X,\pi_*\mathcal G')\cong H^p(X',\mathcal G')$. This is $B$-linear: multiplication by $b\in B$ on $\mathcal G'$ pushes forward to multiplication by the corresponding section of $\mathcal B$ on $\mathcal G$, and the edge map is induced by the identity $\pi$-map, so its naturality with respect to this endomorphism identifies the two actions [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap]. Thus $H^p(X,\mathcal G)$ is finite over $B$.

source.place: Lemma 0897, proof lines 5296-5300; Cohomology of Schemes 089W and 02O6

proof.text: The proper scheme $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-cohomology-direct-sum] applied to the family $(\mathcal G_m)_{m\ge0}$ identifies $H^p(X,\mathcal G)$ with $\bigoplus_mH^p(X,\mathcal G_m)=M$. Under this isomorphism the endomorphism of $\mathcal G$ induced by homogeneous $b\in B_k$ has degree-$m$ component $\mu_b^{(m)}$, so functoriality of cohomology [pqf-def-cohomology] makes its action on $M_m$ exactly $H^p(X,\mu_b^{(m)})$. Finite sums of homogeneous elements and of homogeneous cohomology classes give the displayed convolution formula; conditions (i)-(iii) ensure the unit, additivity, and associativity. Thus the isomorphism is $B$-linear, and finite generation of $H^p(X,\mathcal G)$ from step 4 transfers to $M$. The given compatibility formula identifies the supplied action mod with this transferred action: compare on homogeneous scalars and homogeneous cohomology inclusions, then expand arbitrary scalars and vectors into finite sums. Thus the transferred finite set generates for mod itself. No module action is constructed by this lemma.
